attribution: The single-word orbit map reached main separately (PR #217); this record measures it because the end-to-end figures depend on it, and because main carries no written account of it. The factor-base selection fix is the code this record accompanies.

degree_53_shipped_parameters.parameters: docs/ic/params/k0n53-subgroup.json as it ships: full scan, no collection window

the_three_setup_costs.measured_at: K_0/F_2^53, a 15264-point subgroup-orbit base, each in isolation
the_three_setup_costs.note: The orbit map is built twice in a workflow run -- once for the factor-base summary and once inside the log system -- so its cost counted twice. The pair table is genuine O(|F|^2) work: |F|^2/2 point additions and a 1.9 GB sort. It is now the dominant fixed cost, and unlike the scanning it does not grow with r.

pair_sum_table_seconds.note: untouched; the difference is run-to-run noise

what_changed.same_answer_because: An abscissa carries at most two points, so 2*|abscissae| bounds what a representative set can yield. While that bound is below the target a build could only have come back short and the loop would have gone round again, so skipping it changes nothing. The base is the same 15264 points and 144 columns.
what_changed.what: subgroup base selection stops rebuilding what it has already built
what_changed.why: It rebuilt the whole base after every batch of eight abscissae -- 954 rebuilds over a growing list to reach 15264 points -- which is quadratic in the abscissae.

what_changed.same_answer_because: The general map canonicalises and sorts by point_key = (x+1, y) lexicographically. FastPoint::pack is ((x+1) << 1 | sign) where sign marks which of y and x^y is larger, so within one abscissa it separates P from -P in the same order y does. The two orders agree, so the two maps pick the same representatives, and a test compares them point for point at degrees 15, 19, 31 and 37.
what_changed.why: It projects every base point by the cofactor and then walks each one's whole signed Frobenius orbit -- about 1.6 million point operations at this size -- in big-integer arithmetic.

what_this_is: Once relation collection reached its floor, the logarithm precompute was no longer dominated by collecting -- it was dominated by three fixed setup costs of about eight seconds each. Two were accidental. This records both and measures what removing them buys.
what_this_is_not: Not an algorithmic result: no cost law changed, two implementations of the same computation got faster.
Not a change to the descent or to rho, whose per-target costs move only by run-to-run noise.
Not a claim about any curve in use: K_0 over F_2^53 has a 45-bit subgroup.
Not a measurement of the collection window, which landed separately and is selected on its own run; the end-to-end figures here use the full scan.
The 'with the orbit map alone' row is arithmetic on the isolated measurements, not a separate end-to-end run.
